summary: Little Black Rock lookout site, Umpqua NF: L-5 cab built 1930, removed or destroyed 1966, emergency station lookout in 1935; no source read describes the site today.

facts.status_note: Cab removed in 1966; no source read describes what remains on the ground.

visit.trail_note: Forest Service trail 1562, called Little Black Rock, 0.7 miles (trail guide using USFS data). No source read ties it to the old lookout ground.

events.note: L-5 cab built (register); firelookout.com gives the same year

George Norman, lookout at the Little Black Rock emergency station, kept radio contact with Diamond Rock during an August 1935 emergency, when the telephone line was out and a storm caused static and other interference on the radio
Registered on the Former Fire Lookout Sites register on March 25, 2011

evidence.supports: Built 1930 as an L-5 cab, removed 1966
evidence.quote: Built in 1930, this L-5 cab was removed in 1966.

evidence.quote: The telephone line between Little Black Rock and Diamond Rock, in the South Umpqua District, was put out of commission.

evidence.quote: static and other interference occasioned by the storm

evidence.supports: George Norman as lookout at the emergency station, in contact with Diamond Rock

resolved_conflicts.explanation: The register says the cab was removed in 1966; firelookout.com says it was destroyed that year. Same year, different wording; the story reports both.

sources.title: Little Black Rock Fire Lookout Cabin

notes_for_editor: Site today: no source read describes remains or public status. A Forest Service trail page (fs.usda.gov recarea, recid 63838, actid 50) appeared in search with a snippet saying the lookout is gone and the trail leads to the former site, but the cached page did not contain that text, so it is not quoted. An editor who can read that page could add a site-today sentence. The ORWW Osbornes Project page for Little Black Rock (orww.org/Osbornes_Project/Douglas/Little_Black_Rock/index.html) mentions 2010 documentary photos of current conditions but no text on remains. A 1933 item on the Oregon Lookouts page plans a 10 x 10 CCC lookout; it is not clearly this site, so it is left out. The panorama date differs (August 5, 1936 on the Oregon Lookouts page, August 7 on the ORWW index), so it is not used. No photos added: no image URLs were read.
